verdicts.reason: The two are nearly identical. A's logo, headline and CTA sit on a shared vertical axis inside the circle, and its bottle is bigger and better balanced. In B the logo floats left of the text block's centre, so the right column is less aligned. Both shrink the legal line to an unreadable size and let a background dot sit right against 'hour'.

A's headline is jammed about 18px from the left edge. Its CTA is indented and lines up with nothing, the logo floats at its own x position, and the legal text hugs the bottom-left corner. B keeps comfortable margins and a coherent right text column, though its logo is off-axis and its legal line is unreadably small.

B runs the one-line headline almost to the right edge (about 26px margin) and across the circle's edge. It also shrinks the bottle to a minor element stranded on the left, leaves dead space around it, and places the CTA off the headline's axis. A has clear two-line hierarchy, a well-sized product and better margins, though its legal text is too small to read.

A's one-line headline starts only about 18px from the left edge. Its logo and CTA share no edge or axis with the headline, and the legal text is pushed into the bottom-left corner. B breaks the headline into 'Bottled golden / hour', leaving 'hour' as an orphan, and also misaligns the CTA and logo against the headline. Both shrink the bottle to a secondary element.
